newsitem.title: USA: Albright calls for Arafat to take action.
newsitem.headline: Albright calls for Arafat to take action.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Thursday called on Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to give a "red light" to stop violent acts against Israel.
"What we think is that it is very important for Chairman Arafat to give a red light to the terrorist activities," Albright said in a radio interview.

As Albright spoke, U.S. envoy Dennis Ross was carrying messages to Arafat in Morocco and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel to try to defuse tension and get peace talks back on track following a suicide bombing in Tel Aviv last week.
She told National Public Radio interviewer Diane Rehm that Arafat needed to make a "100 percent effort" to try to halt the violence.
While Arafat had condemned the bombing, she said, there had to be "no perception that he is in any way allowing terrorist acts to go forward, so we think he needs to give a red light on that."

Albright also elaborated on comments she made about Iraq in a speech at Georgetown University in Washington, affirming U.S. intentions to improve ties with a new government in Baghdad should President Saddam Hussein fall from power.
Asked if she had been seeking Saddam's overthrow, Albright said "we're not telling the people of Iraq to do anything."
She said Washington was trying to indicate that the tough policy of seeking to ensure that Iraq lived up to its obligations under United Nations resolutions would stay in place.
The United States was prepared for a dialogue with a successor regime, but it too would have to abide by the U.N. terms, she said.
Albright said the problem with Saddam was that "he has just plain-out lied to the international community about what he has in weapons of mass destruction."
"I think it is very hard for a congenital liar to prove that he is now telling the truth," she said. "The burden of proof is on him."
